message.content: Project: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 (meeting-room booking app; Node 22, built-ins only). Spec: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/spec.md (read the "API" and "Booking rules" sections). Server: server.mjs. Write ONE new test file: /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.rules.test.mjs. Do NOT edit server.mjs, other tests, or the helper. Skill to load: none needed (tdd style: tests only). Use the shared helper /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/helpers/server-harness.mjs (read it): `boot(t)` -> {port,...}, `post(port, objOrString|Buffer, headers?)`, `request(port, method, path, {headers, body})`, `rawRequest(port, rawString|Buffer)` (raw TCP; include `Connection: close` and a correct Content-Length), `valid(over)`, `assertError(res, status, message)` (checks status, exact {error} body AND exact content-type), JSON_TYPE. Use `import { test } from 'node:test'` and `node:assert/strict`. Boot one server per test (each test independent). Keep the file under ~400 lines, functions under 50 lines; table-driven loops are welcome; use exact equality (assert.equal / deepEqual), never regex/prefix. No console.log. Every assert in a loop must carry a message naming the case. Cases to cover (messages are exact spec text): 1. Content-Type (rule 1, 415 'content type must be application/json'): accept (201, use distinct times per booking so no 409): 'Application/JSON ; charset=x', 'application/json;', 'APPLICATION/JSON', and via rawRequest a header `Content-Type:\tapplication/json\t;x` (tab padding). Reject 415: missing header, '' (empty value; send via rawRequest `Content-Type: \r\n`), 'application/json-patch', 'application/jsonx', 'text/json', 'application/json, text/plain', ';application/json', 'application/ json', 'application /json'. Also via rawRequest with a Buffer header line where the value is byte 0xA0 + 'application/json' (non-breaking space padding, latin1 byte) -> 415 (only spaces/tabs are stripped). 2. Rule order: bad content-type + 20000-byte body -> 415; json content-type + 10001-byte invalid JSON -> 413 'body too large'; 10001 bytes of otherwise valid booking JSON (pad with spaces) -> 413; a 10000-byte valid booking body -> 201; multi-byte: a valid booking JSON padded so it is 9990 characters but more than 10000 bytes (use 'é' chars in an extra key value, e.g. {"pad":"éé..."}) -> 413, and assert Buffer.byteLength > 10000 while string length <= 10000 in the test itself; a 10000-byte body made with multi-byte chars (exactly 10000 bytes) -> 201. Chunked upload (http.request with header 'transfer-encoding: chunked', write 10001 bytes in 3 writes) -> 413; chunked 10000-byte valid body -> 201. Invalid room + invalid title -> room message; invalid title + invalid date -> title message; invalid date + invalid start -> date message; invalid start + invalid end -> start message; invalid end + end end message; overlapping AND end<=start -> 400 'end must be after start' not 409; invalid JSON + bad room irrelevant. 3. Rule 3 (400 'body must be a JSON object'): '', ' ', 'null', '[]', '[{}]', '"x"', '0', 'false', '{', '{"room":"Aurora"} x', a UTF-8 BOM (bytes EF BB BF) followed by a fully valid booking JSON -> 400 body message. Whitespace around a valid booking ('\n {..} \n') -> 201. '{}' -> 400 room message. A body whose title contains an invalid UTF-8 byte (Buffer.concat of '{"room":"Aurora","title":"x', Buffer.from([0xff]), '","date":"2026-11-03","start":"10:00","end":"11:00"}') -> 201 with title 'x�'. Invalid byte 0xff inside room -> 400 room message. 4. Rule 4 room: 'aurora', 'AURORA', ' Aurora', 'Aurora ', 'Aurora\u0000', null, 1, ['Aurora'], missing, 'Nebula' -> 400 'room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos'. 'Borealis' and 'Cosmos' -> 201. Body {"__proto__":{"room":"Aurora"}, title,date,start,end} sent as raw JSON string -> 400 room message. 5. Rule 5 title (400 'title must be 1 to 80 characters'): '', ' ', '\t\n', '　 ', null, 5, ['x'], missing, 'x'.repeat(81), ' '+'x'.repeat(81)+' ', '😀'.repeat(41) (82 code units), 'a'.repeat(79)+'😀' (81 units, 80 code points). Accepted (201) with the exact stored title: '😀'.repeat(40) (80 units) kept as is; 'x'.repeat(80) padded with spaces/tabs both sides -> 'x'.repeat(80); '　hi ' -> 'hi'; '﻿hi ' -> 'hi'; ' a b ' -> 'a b' (inner spaces kept); ' hi' -> 'hi' AND 'hi ' -> 'hi' (both ends); '​' (zero-width space, not trimmed by String.prototype.trim) -> 201 title '​'; 'x' stored unchanged. Check the 201 body deepEqual {id, ...fields with trimmed title} and that GET /api/bookings returns the trimmed title. 6. Rule 6 date (400 'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'). Accepted (201): '2000-01-01', '2099-12-31', '2024-02-29', '2000-02-29', '2096-02-29', '2026-01-31', '2026-04-30', '2026-12-31', '2026-11-30'. Rejected: '1999-12-31', '2100-01-01', '2100-02-29', '2023-02-29', '2026-02-29', '2026-02-30', '2026-04-31', '2026-06-31', '2026-09-31', '2026-11-31', '2026-00-10', '2026-11-00', '2026-13-01', '2026-11-3', '26-11-03', '2026/11/03', '20261103', ' 2026-11-03', '2026-11-03 ', '2026-11-03\n', '２０２６-11-03' (full-width digits), '٢٠٢٦-11-03' (Arabic-Indic digits), '+2026-11-03', '2026-11-03T00:00', 20261103 (number), null, missing. 7. Rules 7/8 times. Start rejected (400 'start must be HH:MM'): '24:00', '00:60', '9:00', '09:0', '009:00', '0900', '09-00', ' 09:00', '09:00 ', '２３:００', '-1:00', 900, null, missing. Same list for end with 'end must be HH:MM' (use a valid start '00:00'... note: for end use start '00:00'). Accepted: start '00:00' end '00:01'; start '23:58' end '23:59'; start '00:00' end '23:59' (different rooms/dates so no clash). 8. Rule 9: end == start ('10:00'/'10:00') and end < start ('10:00'/'09:59') -> 400 'end must be after start'. 9. Rule 10 overlap: existing Aurora 2026-11-03 10:00-11:00. 201 for 09:00-10:00 and 11:00-12:00 (touching allowed) — but post these into a fresh server each, or check both but mind that 09:00-10:00 then makes later cases clash; simplest: one server per scenario or use different dates per scenario. 409 'room is already booked from 10:00 to 11:00' for: 10:59-11:30, 09:00-10:01, 10:15-10:45 (inside), 09:00-12:00 (enclosing), 10:00-11:00 (identical). Same times in Borealis -> 201; same times on 2026-11-04 -> 201. Earliest-starting: insert (in this order) 11:00-12:00, 10:00-11:00, 09:00-10:00 into Aurora same day, then post 09:30-11:30 -> 409 'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'; post 10:30-11:30 -> 'room is already booked from 10:00 to 11:00'. A deleted booking no longer clashes: DELETE it, then same slot -> 201. Rejected 409 POST does not consume an id: after a 409, the next 201 has id = previous max + 1. 10. 201 reply: content-type exactly JSON_TYPE, body deepEqual {id: 1, room, title, date, start, end} (exact keys), id is a number; second gets id 2. 11. GET /api/bookings ?date query (decoded as URLSearchParams): with bookings on 2026-11-03 (two) and 2026-11-04 (one): '?date=2026%2D11%2D03' -> 200 only the 11-03 ones; '?%64ate=2026-11-03' -> filtered to 11-03 (key is decoded too); '?x=1&date=2026-11-04' -> only 11-04; '?Date=2026-11-03' -> all 3 (other params ignored); '?a=1?date=bad' -> 200 all 3 (query is everything after the first ?); '?date=bad&date=2026-11-03' -> 400; '?date=2026-11-03&date=bad' -> 200 the two; '?date' and '?date=' and '?date&date=2026-11-03' -> 400; '?date=2026-11-03+' and '?date=+2026-11-03' and '?date=2026-11-03%20' -> 400; '?date=2026-02-29' -> 400; '?date=2024-02-29' -> 200 {bookings: []}; '?date=2100-01-01' -> 400; '?date=2099-12-31' -> 200 []. The 400 is exactly assertError(res, 400, 'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'). Check each filtered reply's bookings array deepEqual to the expected objects in sorted order. 12. Sorting: insert out of order bookings across 3 dates, several starts, all rooms with equal date+start in reverse room order (Cosmos, Borealis, Aurora); assert GET order exactly by date, then start, then room order Aurora

content.content: 1 # Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. **The failing case.** The test is `rule 1: accepted media type spellings`, and the failing assertion is the raw-TCP request with header `Content-Type:\tapplication/json\t;x`.
- Expected: status 201.
- Actual: `rawRequest` returned status `NaN`, meaning it got no parseable HTTP status line back (probably an empty response, or the connection closed without a reply).
- The other three accepted spellings, which go through `http.request`, passed. Every other raw-TCP case also passed, including empty value, `0xA0` padding and the `Connection: close` form.
- I can't tell whether this is a server problem or a test problem. It could be Node's HTTP parser (llhttp) rejecting or dropping the connection on a tab-padded value, which would be a server-side violation of the spec. It could also be a quirk in how my `rawPost` helper builds the request. I did not weaken or remove the case.

I probed the case twice with a throwaway script and `nc` against a running server. Both commands were denied, so the cause is still unconfirmed. If you want it narrowed down, the next step is to dump the raw bytes the server sends back for that request.

**Other things to know.**
- The other 24 tests passed, including all the 413 byte-count and chunked cases, the BOM and invalid-UTF-8 cases, rule order, and the `?date` query parsing. I saw no other server spec violations.
- I used a local `expectError` helper instead of the harness's `assertError`, because the harness version has no per-case message and you asked for a message on every assert in a loop.
- I did not edit `server.mjs`, other tests, or the helper. I created `/tmp/probe.mjs` (the throwaway probe script) and did not delete it.
